result:
Inland rivers and their regional lakes are now withdrawn from the app, committed as `944e2d9` on `opus/disable-rivers-20260928`. The starting HEAD was `e0d9d9c` as required, and nothing was pushed. Oceans, dry-ground landing and walking, forests and fauna, and the other controls still work. The change passes its focused tests, typecheck and build. Browser/WebGL visual checks were not run.

**How it's switched off:** a new file, `src/inland-rivers.ts`, is the one switch, and it's off in the app. Everything that used to read a body's river data now goes through it, so leftover river data attached to a body has no effect:
- **Terrain:** the terrain sampler uses no river regions by default. There's no channel or lake-bowl carving, no inland wetness and no bank colouring. Terrain tiles also skip the river-bed shaping. Surface queries now report water only where the dated ocean is. Passing river regions to the sampler explicitly still runs the old algorithm, for archival tests.
- **Renderer:** no river water, bank dressing or lake reflection. The fine-grained contact level used near rivers is gone, and waiting for river generation no longer blocks landing or walking.
- **Generation:** focusing or approaching a body never starts the river worker, and the worker isn't included in the build any more.
- **`main.ts`:** removed Find rivers, the Drainage atlas, river sites, river flight, river/drainage exports, the automatic river pick on focus, and `?river=` restore.
- **Old `?river=` links:** they open the ordinary body view with the notice: "Inland rivers and their regional lakes are currently unavailable. This river link opens the ordinary world instead." The parameter disappears the next time the URL is written.

**Versions:** terrain goes from `terrain-1.5.0` to `terrain-1.6.0`, surface to `atlas-surface-7-no-inland-rivers`, and the build version to `atlas-client-2026-09-28-no-inland-rivers-1`. I didn't add a separate river version field. Bookmarks saved with the older terrain or surface version show the existing "older … model versions" notice, which now also says inland rivers and their regional lakes are unavailable.

**Lakes:** confirmed coupled. The only inland lakes are the ones built inside each river region by `river-generation.ts`, and there's no separate lake catalogue. So those lakes are disabled together with the rivers, and the in-app help, guide pages, README and a new `docs/inland-rivers-withdrawn-2026-09-28.md` say so. Oceans are unaffected.

**Tests:** the new `tests/inland-rivers-disabled.test.mjs` (9 tests, added to `npm test`) covers:
- Surface samples, the orbit preview and tiles on a real planet are identical with and without the river data attached. There's no wetness, carving or bank colour, and a check first confirms those same points really are on river or lake water under the old algorithm.
- An ocean point is still dated, wet and not walkable after the ocean forms, and has no ocean before it forms.
- Focusing a water world never starts a river worker, and readiness is reported true.
- A renderer check: a body still carrying river data gets no river or reflection mesh, and ordinary contact terrain for landing becomes available at the normal level. The old code fails this, because it blocks until the river build finishes.
- The version and `?river=` notices, plus a source check that `main.ts` no longer reads or writes `river=` and that no app code turns the old river pipeline back on.

The old river test files (`river-terrain`, `river-determinism`, `river-environment`, and one case in `forest-water-validity`) now explicitly switch the old river code back on for their own run. Their assertions are unchanged except one pinned terrain version string.

**Commands run:**
- `node --test` on the new file, all 8 `river-*.test.mjs` files, `drainage`, `world-surface`, `terrain-water-refresh`, `forest-*`, `planet-*`, `surface`, `ground`, `catalog`, `creature-contact`, `time-nav`, `time-integration`, `acceptance/{version-compat,existence-gating,visit-order-independence,t-seek-independence}` and `golden/perturbation`: everything passes except three failures that already exist on the baseline:
  - `version-compat`'s version table still expects `atlas-history-2`.
  - `time-nav` "horizon gating".
  - A cosmology "scaleFactorAt saturation" test.

  All three involve only cosmology and history code that this change doesn't touch.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: passes.
- `npm run build`: passes (`dist/` is ignored by git).
- `git diff --check`: clean.

**Changed files (21):**
- **Code:** `src/inland-rivers.ts` (new), `src/terrain.ts`, `src/planet-tiles.ts`, `src/world-surface.ts`, `src/planet-renderer.ts`, `src/hydrology-registry.ts`, `src/main.ts`, `src/time-nav.ts`
- **Tests:** `tests/inland-rivers-disabled.test.mjs` (new), `tests/river-terrain.test.mjs`, `tests/river-determinism.test.mjs`, `tests/river-environment.test.mjs`, `tests/forest-water-validity.test.mjs`, `package.json` (test script only)
- **Docs and UI text:** `README.md`, `index.html`, `docs/inland-rivers-withdrawn-2026-09-28.md` (new), `docs/continuous-planet-detail.md`, `guide/index.html`, `guide/travel.html`, `guide/water-atmosphere.html`

No river source modules or historical tests were deleted. The biosphere model's "river-corridor" habitat name is a species habitat label, not rendered geography, so I left it as is.
